problems.source_says: Not supported as coded. The paper says four 'student groups' were randomly assigned. It never calls them classes, course sections, or intact groups. A text-layer search of all 14 pages finds 'class' only in 'intraclass', 'classification', and 'GPT-4-class'. The form's own what_was_assigned says the paper does not say whether the groups were existing course sections. 'class' is an inference from recruitment through a mandatory course (p. 3) and the five lecturers thanked (p. 13). The text supports assignment by group, two groups per arm, of unstated origin. Suggested coding: unit 'other', with what_was_assigned naming the unit as 'student group (four groups, two per arm; the paper does not say how they were formed)'. Criterion 1 is not affected.
problems.quote: the design task was carried out with four student groups, randomly assigned to two predefined conditions
problems.locator: p. 4, Section 3.2.2; p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 13, Acknowledgments; text-layer search of pp. 1-14 for class, intact, cohort, grupo, section, course, lecturer

confirmed.statement: The document states random assignment, once: four student groups were 'randomly assigned to two predefined conditions', sketch groups A+C (n=31) and AI groups B+D (n=30). The form's assignment quote is verbatim and its locator is right. The paper describes no randomization procedure, randomizer, or stratification.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3.2.2; text-layer search of pp. 1-14 for random, assign, cluster, session

confirmed.statement: Assignment is by group, not by person: four groups, two per arm. Students then worked alone on the same brief. Structure 'between' is right, and there is no within-person order to check.

What was assigned is generative-AI access for the student's own design work, not a change in whose output is evaluated. AI groups used their own laptops or smartphones and AI tools of their choice. Sketch groups could not use any devices. Figure 1 labels the arms 'task with AI' and 'task without AI'.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3.2.2 and Figure 2; p. 3, Figure 1

confirmed.statement: The tools are generative AI: LLM chatbots (ChatGPT GPT-4o free n=23, GPT-4o Plus n=2, DeepSeek-R1 n=3, Copilot n=3, Gemini 2.5 n=1) and text-to-image platforms (Leonardo.AI n=15, Krea.AI n=8, Meshy.AI n=2, Vizcom n=2, PromeAI, ArtGuru, and GenCraft n=1 each). The form's name_model list matches the page. 28 of 30 AI students made their images from a prompt that the LLM wrote, so role open_chat, with image generation described in how_used, fits.

The comparison arm matches the form (ai none, ai_vs_bau): pen and paper, no devices, and no search engines, magazines, or other material. The paper calls the sketch groups control groups and the AI groups experimental groups.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3.2.2; p. 12, Section 5.4; p. 3, Figure 1 caption; p. 10, Section 4.3

confirmed.statement: Nothing in the text contradicts random assignment. The remark that 'the study was not conducted in a controlled environment' is about the free choice of AI models. The paper lists 'student distribution' among possible reasons the two t-tests disagree, which fits assignment of few groups.
preregistered = not_stated is right. Text-layer searches for regist, osf, and aspredicted find only 'registering each prompt'.
The AUT range counts sum to 68 (25 + 36 + 7), not 61. The form records this in notes. The text says nothing about students lost between assignment and the design task.

summary: The PDF supports the core assignment coding: four student groups were randomly assigned, two to pen-and-paper sketching with no devices (31 students) and two to free use of LLM chatbots and text-to-image tools for their own design work (30 students), so criterion 1 holds as group-level random assignment with no stated procedure (p. 4, Section 3.2.2). The refutation rests only on assignment.unit = class: the paper says 'student groups' and never says they were classes or course sections, so 'other' is the code the text supports.
